correctness.rationale: For every n>=2,t>=1,ell>=1, the contribution of a four-good block is at most one unless all four goods go to agent 1. With h whole blocks, EF-ell forces (n-1)(h-ell)<=t-h, while EFX forces (n-1)h<=t-h by deleting a primed good in a whole block. Explicit complete allocations achieve both floor bounds. A separate allocation is exactly EF with optimum t+floor(t/n); unrestricted optimum is 2t. A standalone exhaustive implementation checked 1,722,355 small complete allocations and matched all formulas, but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is an exact mathematical optimization invariant of the canonical asymptotic fairness obstruction in new 2026 literature. It computes, for all n,t,ell, the precise welfare loss and the zero-extra-cost equality of strong EF and EFX, identifies a sharp one-unit gain under EF1 precisely for n not dividing t, and provides constructive attaining allocations. Such exact phase thresholds are useful for calibration of fair-complement algorithms and clarify what the original asymptotic example actually demonstrates. It does not purport to prove a general SPOC price-of-fairness theorem.
